NASB.1: Woe to the bloody city, completely full of lies [and] pillage; [Her] prey never departs.
NASB.2: The noise of the whip, The noise of the rattling of the wheel, Galloping horses And bounding chariots!
NASB.3: Horsemen charging, Swords flashing, spears gleaming, Many slain, a mass of corpses, And countless dead bodies-- They stumble over the dead bodies!
NASB.4: [All] because of the many harlotries of the harlot, The charming one, the mistress of sorceries, Who sells nations by her harlotries And families by her sorceries.
NASB.5: 'Behold, I am against you,' declares the LORD of hosts; 'And I will lift up your skirts over your face, And show to the nations your nakedness And to the kingdoms your disgrace.
NASB.6: 'I will throw filth on you And make you vile, And set you up as a spectacle.
NASB.7: 'And it will come about that all who see you Will shrink from you and say, 'Nineveh is devastated! Who will grieve for her?' Where will I seek comforters for you?'
NASB.8: Are you better than No-amon, Which was situated by the waters of the Nile, With water surrounding her, Whose rampart [was] the sea, Whose wall [consisted] of the sea?
NASB.9: Ethiopia was [her] might, And Egypt too, without limits. Put and Lubim were among her helpers.
NASB.10: Yet she became an exile, She went into captivity; Also her small children were dashed to pieces At the head of every street; They cast lots for her honorable men, And all her great men were bound with fetters.
NASB.11: You too will become drunk, You will be hidden. You too will search for a refuge from the enemy.
NASB.12: All your fortifications are fig trees with ripe fruit-- When shaken, they fall into the eater's mouth.
NASB.13: Behold, your people are women in your midst! The gates of your land are opened wide to your enemies; Fire consumes your gate bars.
NASB.14: Draw for yourself water for the siege! Strengthen your fortifications! Go into the clay and tread the mortar! Take hold of the brick mold!
NASB.15: There fire will consume you, The sword will cut you down; It will consume you as the locust [does]. Multiply yourself like the creeping locust, Multiply yourself like the swarming locust.
NASB.16: You have increased your traders more than the stars of heaven-- The creeping locust strips and flies away.
NASB.17: Your guardsmen are like the swarming locust. Your marshals are like hordes of grasshoppers Settling in the stone walls on a cold day. The sun rises and they flee, And the place where they are is not known.
NASB.18: Your shepherds are sleeping, O king of Assyria; Your nobles are lying down. Your people are scattered on the mountains And there is no one to regather [them].
NASB.19: There is no relief for your breakdown, Your wound is incurable. All who hear about you Will clap [their] hands over you, For on whom has not your evil passed continually?

NKJV.1: Woe to the bloody city! It is all full of lies and robbery. Its victim never departs.
NKJV.2: The noise of a whip And the noise of rattling wheels, Of galloping horses, Of clattering chariots!
NKJV.3: Horsemen charge with bright sword and glittering spear. There is a multitude of slain, A great number of bodies, Countless corpses— They stumble over the corpses—
NKJV.4: Because of the multitude of harlotries of the seductive harlot,  The mistress of sorceries, Who sells nations through her harlotries, And families through her sorceries.
NKJV.5: “Behold, I am against you,” says the LORD of hosts; “I will lift your skirts over your face, I will show the nations your nakedness, And the kingdoms your shame.
NKJV.6: I will cast abominable filth upon you, Make you vile, And make you a spectacle.
NKJV.7: It shall come to pass that all who look upon you Will flee from you, and say, ‘Nineveh is laid waste! Who will bemoan her?’ Where shall I seek comforters for you?”
NKJV.8: Are you better than No Amon That was situated by the River, That had the waters around her, Whose rampart was the sea, Whose wall was the sea?
NKJV.9: Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, And it was boundless; Put and Lubim were your helpers.
NKJV.10: Yet she was carried away, She went into captivity; Her young children also were dashed to pieces At the head of every street; They cast lots for her honorable men, And all her great men were bound in chains.
NKJV.11: You also will be drunk; You will be hidden; You also will seek refuge from the enemy.
NKJV.12: All your strongholds are fig trees with ripened figs: If they are shaken, They fall into the mouth of the eater.
NKJV.13: Surely, your people in your midst are women! The gates of your land are wide open for your enemies; Fire shall devour the bars of your gates.
NKJV.14: Draw your water for the siege!  Fortify your strongholds! Go into the clay and tread the mortar! Make strong the brick kiln!
NKJV.15: There the fire will devour you, The sword will cut you off; It will eat you up like a locust. Make yourself many—like the locust! Make yourself many— like the swarming locusts!
NKJV.16: You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of heaven. The locust plunders and flies away.
NKJV.17: Your commanders are like swarming locusts, And your generals like great grasshoppers, Which camp in the hedges on a cold day; When the sun rises they flee away, And the place where they are is not known.
NKJV.18: Your shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria; Your nobles rest in the dust. Your people are scattered on the mountains, And no one gathers them.
NKJV.19: Your injury has no healing, Your wound is severe. All who hear news of you Will clap their hands over you, For upon whom has not your wickedness passed continually?

ESV.1: Woe to the bloody city, all full of lies and plunder — no end to the prey!
ESV.2: The crack of the whip, and rumble of the wheel, galloping horse and bounding chariot!
ESV.3: Horsemen charging, flashing sword and glittering spear, hosts of slain, heaps of corpses, dead bodies without end — they stumble over the bodies!
ESV.4: And all for the countless whorings of the prostitute, graceful and of deadly charms, who betrays nations with her whorings, and peoples with her charms.
ESV.5: Behold, I am against you, declares the LORD of hosts, and will lift up your skirts over your face; and I will make nations look at your nakedness and kingdoms at your shame.
ESV.6: I will throw filth at you and treat you with contempt and make you a spectacle.
ESV.7: And all who look at you will shrink from you and say, “Wasted is Nineveh; who will grieve for her?” Where shall I seek comforters for you?
ESV.8: Are you better than Thebes  that sat by the Nile, with water around her, her rampart a sea, and water her wall?
ESV.9: Cush was her strength; Egypt too, and that without limit; Put and the Libyans were her  helpers.
ESV.10: Yet she became an exile; she went into captivity; her infants were dashed in pieces at the head of every street; for her honored men lots were cast, and all her great men were bound in chains.
ESV.11: You also will be drunken; you will go into hiding; you will seek a refuge from the enemy.
ESV.12: All your fortresses are like fig trees with first-ripe figs — if shaken they fall into the mouth of the eater.
ESV.13: Behold, your troops are women in your midst. The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire has devoured your bars.
ESV.14: Draw water for the siege; strengthen your forts; go into the clay; tread the mortar; take hold of the brick mold!
ESV.15: There will the fire devour you; the sword will cut you off. It will devour you like the locust. Multiply yourselves like the locust; multiply like the grasshopper!
ESV.16: You increased your merchants more than the stars of the heavens. The locust spreads its wings and flies away.
ESV.17: Your princes are like grasshoppers, your scribes  like clouds of locusts settling on the fences in a day of cold — when the sun rises, they fly away; no one knows where they are.
ESV.18: Your shepherds are asleep, O king of Assyria; your nobles slumber. Your people are scattered on the mountains with none to gather them.
ESV.19: There is no easing your hurt; your wound is grievous. All who hear the news about you clap their hands over you. For upon whom has not come your unceasing evil?

WEB.1: Woe to the bloody city! It is all full of lies and robbery. The prey doesn’t depart.
WEB.2: The noise of the whip, the noise of the rattling of wheels, prancing horses, and bounding chariots,
WEB.3: the horseman mounting, and the flashing sword, the glittering spear, and a multitude of slain, and a great heap of corpses, and there is no end of the bodies. They stumble on their bodies,
WEB.4: because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations through her prostitution, and families through her witchcraft.
WEB.5: “Behold, I am against you,” says Yahweh of Armies, “and I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show the nations your nakedness, and the kingdoms your shame.
WEB.6: I will throw abominable filth on you, and make you vile, and will set you a spectacle.
WEB.7: It will happen that all those who look at you will flee from you, and say, ‘Nineveh is laid waste! Who will mourn for her?’ Where will I seek comforters for you?”
WEB.8: Are you better than No-Amon,  who was situated among the rivers, who had the waters around her; whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was of the sea?
WEB.9: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength. Put and Libya were her helpers.
WEB.10: Yet was she carried away. She went into captivity. Her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of all the streets, and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
WEB.11: You also will be drunken. You will be hidden. You also will seek a stronghold because of the enemy.
WEB.12: All your fortresses will be like fig trees with the first-ripe figs: if they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
WEB.13: Behold, your troops among you are women. The gates of your land are set wide open to your enemies. The fire has devoured your bars.
WEB.14: Draw water for the siege. Strengthen your fortresses. Go into the clay, and tread the mortar. Make the brick kiln strong.
WEB.15: There the fire will devour you. The sword will cut you off. It will devour you like the grasshopper. Multiply like grasshoppers. Multiply like the locust.
WEB.16: You have increased your merchants more than the stars of the skies. The grasshopper strips, and flees away.
WEB.17: Your guards are like the locusts, and your officials like the swarms of locusts, which settle on the walls on a cold day, but when the sun appears, they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.
WEB.18: Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria. Your nobles lie down. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
WEB.19: There is no healing your wound, for your injury is fatal. All who hear the report of you clap their hands over you; for who hasn’t felt your endless cruelty?

NLT.1:
What sorrow awaits Nineveh,
the city of murder and lies!
She is crammed with wealth
and is never without victims.
NLT.2:
Hear the crack of whips,
the rumble of wheels!
Horses’ hooves pound,
and chariots clatter wildly.
NLT.3:
See the flashing swords and glittering spears
as the charioteers charge past!
There are countless casualties,
heaps of bodies —
so many bodies that
people stumble over them.
NLT.4:
All this because Nineveh,
the beautiful and faithless city,
mistress of deadly charms,
enticed the nations with her beauty.
She taught them all her magic,
enchanting people everywhere.
NLT.5:
“I am your enemy!”
says the LORD of Heaven’s Armies.
“And now I will lift your skirts
and show all the earth your nakedness and shame.
NLT.6:
I will cover you with filth
and show the world how vile you really are.
NLT.7:
All who see you will shrink back and say,
‘Nineveh lies in ruins.
Where are the mourners?’
Does anyone regret your destruction?”
NLT.8:
Are you any better than the city of Thebes,
situated on the Nile River, surrounded by water?
She was protected by the river on all sides,
walled in by water.
NLT.9:
Ethiopia and the land of Egypt
gave unlimited assistance.
The nations of Put and Libya
were among her allies.
NLT.10:
Yet Thebes fell,
and her people were led away as captives.
Her babies were dashed to death
against the stones of the streets.
Soldiers threw dice to get Egyptian officers as servants.
All their leaders were bound in chains.
NLT.11:
And you, Nineveh, will also stagger like a drunkard.
You will hide for fear of the attacking enemy.
NLT.12:
All your fortresses will fall.
They will be devoured like the ripe figs
that fall into the mouths
of those who shake the trees.
NLT.13:
Your troops will be as weak
and helpless as women.
The gates of your land will be opened wide to the enemy
and set on fire and burned.
NLT.14:
Get ready for the siege!
Store up water!
Strengthen the defenses!
Go into the pits to trample clay,
and pack it into molds,
making bricks to repair the walls.
NLT.15:
But the fire will devour you;
the sword will cut you down.
The enemy will consume you like locusts,
devouring everything they see.
There will be no escape,
even if you multiply like swarming locusts.
NLT.16:
Your merchants have multiplied
until they outnumber the stars.
But like a swarm of locusts,
they strip the land and fly away.
NLT.17:
Your guards and officials are also like swarming locusts
that crowd together in the hedges on a cold day.
But like locusts that fly away when the sun comes up,
all of them will fly away and disappear.
NLT.18:
Your shepherds are asleep, O Assyrian king;
your princes lie dead in the dust.
Your people are scattered across the mountains
with no one to gather them together.
NLT.19:
There is no healing for your wound;
your injury is fatal.
All who hear of your destruction
will clap their hands for joy.
Where can anyone be found
who has not suffered from your continual cruelty?

AMP.1:
Woe (judgment is coming) to the city of blood [guilty of murder and mayhem], completely full of lies and pillage;
Her prey never departs [alive].
AMP.2:
The noise of the [cracking of the] whip,
The noise of the rattling of the wheel,
Galloping horses
And rumbling and bounding chariots [in the assault of Nineveh]!
AMP.3:
Horsemen charging,
Swords flashing, spears gleaming,
Many slain, a mass of corpses,
No end of corpses—
The horsemen stumble over the corpses!
AMP.4:
All because of the many acts of prostitution of [Nineveh] the prostitute,
The charming and well-favored one, the mistress of sorceries,
Who betrays nations by her acts of prostitution (idolatry)
And families by her sorceries.
AMP.5:
"Behold, I am against you," declares the LORD of hosts,
"And I will lift up your skirts over your face,
And I will let the nations look at your nakedness [O Nineveh]
And the kingdoms at your disgrace.
AMP.6:
"I will throw filth on you
And make you vile and treat you with contempt,
And set you up as a spectacle.
AMP.7:
"And it will come about that all who see you
Will shrink back and run from you and say,
'Nineveh is completely ruined!
Who will grieve for her?'
Where will I seek comforters for you?"
AMP.8:
Are you better than Thebes,
Which was situated by the waters of the Nile,
With water surrounding her,
Whose defense was the sea (the Nile),
Whose wall consisted of the sea?
AMP.9:
Ethiopia was her strength,
And Egypt too, without limits.
Put and Lubim were among her helpers.
AMP.10:
Yet she became an exile;
She went into captivity.
Her young children were dashed to pieces
At the head of every street;
They cast lots for her honorable men,
And all her great men were bound with chains.
AMP.11:
You too [Nineveh] will become drunk [with the cup of God's wrath];
You will be hidden.
You too [Nineveh] will search [in vain] for a refuge from the enemy.
AMP.12:
All your fortresses are [nothing but] fig trees with ripe figs—
When shaken they fall into the mouth of the eater.
AMP.13:
Behold, your people are [as weak and helpless as] women in your midst!
The gates of your land are opened wide to your enemies;
Fire consumes the bars across your gates.
AMP.14:
Draw water for a [long, continued] siege!
Strengthen your fortresses!
Go down to the clay pits, trample the mortar!
Prepare the brick kiln [to burn bricks for the rampart]!
AMP.15:
But there [in the very midst of these preparations] the fire will devour you;
The sword will cut you down;
It will devour you as the locust does.
Multiply yourself like the creeping locusts;
Multiply yourself like the swarming locusts.
AMP.16:
You have increased your traders more than the [visible] stars of heaven—
The creeping locust strips and destroys and then flies away.
AMP.17:
Your guardsmen are like the swarming locusts.
Your marshals are like the hordes of grasshoppers
Settling in the stone walls on a cold day.
When the sun rises, they fly away,
And no one knows the place where they are.
AMP.18:
Your shepherds are asleep, O king of Assyria;
Your nobles are lying down [in death].
Your people are scattered on the mountains
And there is no one to gather them.
AMP.19:
There is no relief and healing for your hurt;
Your wound is incurable.
All who hear the news about you
Clap their hands over [what has happened to] you.
For on whom has your [unceasing] evil not come continually?

NIV.1:
Woe to Nineveh
Woe to the city of blood,
full of lies,
full of plunder,
never without victims!
NIV.2:
The crack of whips,
the clatter of wheels,
galloping horses
and jolting chariots!
NIV.3:
Charging cavalry,
flashing swords
and glittering spears!
Many casualties,
piles of dead,
bodies without number,
people stumbling over the corpses—
NIV.4:
all because of the wanton lust of a harlot,
alluring, the mistress of sorceries,
who enslaved nations by her prostitution
and peoples by her witchcraft.
NIV.5:
“I am against you,” declares the Lord Almighty.
“I will lift your skirts over your face.
I will show the nations your nakedness
and the kingdoms your shame.
NIV.6:
I will pelt you with filth,
I will treat you with contempt
and make you a spectacle.
NIV.7:
All who see you will flee from you and say,
‘Nineveh is in ruins—who will mourn for her?’
Where can I find anyone to comfort you?”
NIV.8:
Are you better than Thebes,
situated on the Nile,
with water around her?
The river was her defense,
the waters her wall.
NIV.9:
Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength;
Put and Libya were among her allies.
NIV.10:
Yet she was taken captive
and went into exile.
Her infants were dashed to pieces
at the head of every street.
Lots were cast for her nobles,
and all her great men were put in chains.
NIV.11:
You too will become drunk;
you will go into hiding
and seek refuge from the enemy.
NIV.12:
All your fortresses are like fig trees
with their first ripe fruit;
when they are shaken,
the figs fall into the mouth of the eater.
NIV.13:
Look at your troops—
they are all women!
The gates of your land
are wide open to your enemies;
fire has consumed their bars.
NIV.14:
Draw water for the siege,
strengthen your defenses!
Work the clay,
tread the mortar,
repair the brickwork!
NIV.15:
There the fire will devour you;
the sword will cut you down
and, like grasshoppers, consume you.
Multiply like grasshoppers,
multiply like locusts!
NIV.16:
You have increased the number of your merchants
till they are more than the stars of the sky,
but like locusts they strip the land
and then fly away.
NIV.17:
Your guards are like locusts,
your officials like swarms of locusts
that settle in the walls on a cold day—
but when the sun appears they fly away,
and no one knows where.
NIV.18:
O king of Assyria, your shepherds slumber;
your nobles lie down to rest.
Your people are scattered on the mountains
with no one to gather them.
NIV.19:
Nothing can heal your wound;
your injury is fatal.
Everyone who hears the news about you
claps his hands at your fall,
for who has not felt
your endless cruelty?

NRSVCE.1:
Ah! City of bloodshed, utterly deceitful, full of booty —
no end to the plunder!
NRSVCE.2:
The crack of whip and rumble of wheel,
galloping horse and bounding chariot!
NRSVCE.3:
Horsemen charging,
flashing sword and glittering spear,
piles of dead,
heaps of corpses,
dead bodies without end —
they stumble over the bodies!
NRSVCE.4:
Because of the countless debaucheries of the prostitute,
gracefully alluring, mistress of sorcery,
who enslaves nations through her debaucheries,
and peoples through her sorcery,
NRSVCE.5:
I am against you,
says the LORD of hosts,
and will lift up your skirts over your face;
and I will let nations look on your nakedness
and kingdoms on your shame.
NRSVCE.6:
I will throw filth at you
and treat you with contempt,
and make you a spectacle.
NRSVCE.7:
Then all who see you will shrink from you and say,
“Nineveh is devastated; who will bemoan her?”
Where shall I seek comforters for you?
NRSVCE.8:
Are you better than Thebes
that sat by the Nile,
with water around her,
her rampart a sea,
water her wall?
NRSVCE.9:
Ethiopia was her strength,
Egypt too, and that without limit;
Put and the Libyans were her helpers.
NRSVCE.10:
Yet she became an exile,
she went into captivity;
even her infants were dashed in pieces
at the head of every street;
lots were cast for her nobles,
all her dignitaries were bound in fetters.
NRSVCE.11:
You also will be drunken,
you will go into hiding;
you will seek
a refuge from the enemy.
NRSVCE.12:
All your fortresses are like fig trees
with first-ripe figs —
if shaken they fall
into the mouth of the eater.
NRSVCE.13:
Look at your troops:
they are women in your midst.
The gates of your land
are wide open to your foes;
fire has devoured the bars of your gates.
NRSVCE.14:
Draw water for the siege,
strengthen your forts;
trample the clay,
tread the mortar,
take hold of the brick mold!
NRSVCE.15:
There the fire will devour you,
the sword will cut you off.
It will devour you like the locust.
Multiply yourselves like the locust,
multiply like the grasshopper!
NRSVCE.16:
You increased your merchants
more than the stars of the heavens.
The locust sheds its skin and flies away.
NRSVCE.17:
Your guards are like grasshoppers,
your scribes like swarms of locusts
settling on the fences
on a cold day —
when the sun rises, they fly away;
no one knows where they have gone.
NRSVCE.18:
Your shepherds are asleep,
O king of Assyria;
your nobles slumber.
Your people are scattered on the mountains
with no one to gather them.
NRSVCE.19:
There is no assuaging your hurt,
your wound is mortal.
All who hear the news about you
clap their hands over you.
For who has ever escaped
your endless cruelty?

MSG.1:
Doom to Murder City—
full of lies, bursting with loot, addicted to violence!
MSG.2:
Horns blaring, wheels clattering,
horses rearing, chariots lurching,
MSG.3:
Horsemen galloping,
brandishing swords and spears,
Dead bodies rotting in the street,
corpses stacked like cordwood,
Bodies in every gutter and alley,
clogging every intersection!
MSG.4:
And whores! Whores without end!
Whore City,
Fatally seductive, you're the Witch of Seduction,
luring nations to their ruin with your evil spells.
MSG.5:
"I'm your enemy, Whore Nineveh—
I, God-of-the-Angel-Armies!
I'll strip you of your seductive silk robes
and expose you on the world stage.
I'll let the nations get their fill of the ugly truth
of who you really are and have been all along.
MSG.6:
I'll pelt you with dog dung
and place you on a pedestal: 'Slut on Exhibit.'
MSG.7:
Everyone who sees you will gag and say,
'Nineveh's a pigsty:
What on earth did we ever see in her?
Who would give her a second look? Ugh!' "
MSG.8:
Do you think you're superior to Egyptian Thebes,
proudly invincible on the River Nile,
Protected by the great River,
walled in by the River, secure?
MSG.9:
Ethiopia stood guard to the south,
Egypt to the north.
Put and Libya, strong friends,
were ready to step in and help.
MSG.10:
But you know what happened to her:
The whole city was marched off to a refugee camp,
Her babies smashed to death
in public view on the streets,
Her prize leaders auctioned off,
her celebrities put in chain gangs.
MSG.11:
Expect the same treatment, Nineveh.
You'll soon be staggering like a bunch of drunks,
Wondering what hit you,
looking for a place to sleep it off.
MSG.12:
All your forts are like peach trees,
the lush peaches ripe, ready for the picking.
One shake of the tree and they fall
straight into hungry mouths.
MSG.13:
Face it: Your warriors are wimps.
You're sitting ducks.
Your borders are gaping doors, inviting
your enemies in. And who's to stop them?
MSG.14:
Store up water for the siege.
Shore up your defenses.
Get down to basics: Work the clay
and make bricks.
MSG.15:
Sorry. Too late.
Enemy fire will burn you up.
Swords will cut you to pieces.
You'll be chewed up as if by locusts.
Yes, as if by locusts—a fitting fate,
for you yourselves are a locust plague.
MSG.16:
You've multiplied shops and shopkeepers—
more buyers and sellers than stars in the sky!
A plague of locusts, cleaning out the neighborhood
and then flying off.
MSG.17:
Your bureaucrats are locusts,
your brokers and bankers are locusts.
Early on, they're all at your service,
full of smiles and promises,
But later when you return with questions or complaints,
you'll find they've flown off and are nowhere to be found.
MSG.18:
King of Assyria! Your shepherd-leaders,
in charge of caring for your people,
Are busy doing everything else but.
They're not doing their job,
And your people are scattered and lost.
There's no one to look after them.
MSG.19:
You're past the point of no return.
Your wound is fatal.
When the story of your fate gets out,
the whole world will applaud and cry "Encore!"
Your cruel evil has seeped
into every nook and cranny of the world.
Everyone has felt it and suffered.

NET.1: Woe to the city guilty of bloodshed! She is full of lies; she is filled with plunder; she has hoarded her spoil!
NET.2: The chariot drivers will crack their whips; the chariot wheels will shake the ground; the chariot horses will gallop; the war chariots will bolt forward!
NET.3: The charioteers will charge ahead; their swords will flash and their spears will glimmer! There will be many people slain; there will be piles of the dead, and countless casualties — so many that people will stumble over the corpses.
NET.4: “Because you have acted like a wanton prostitute — a seductive mistress who practices sorcery, who enslaves nations by her harlotry, and entices peoples by her sorcery —
NET.5: I am against you,” declares the LORD who commands armies. “I will strip off your clothes! I will show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms;
NET.6: I will pelt you with filth; I will treat you with contempt; I will make you a public spectacle.
NET.7: Everyone who sees you will turn away from you in disgust; they will say, ‘Nineveh has been devastated! Who will lament for her?’ There will be no one to comfort you!”
NET.8: You are no more secure than Thebes — she was located on the banks of the Nile; the waters surrounded her, her rampart was the sea, the water was her wall.
NET.9: Cush and Egypt had limitless strength; Put and the Libyans were among her allies.
NET.10: Yet she went into captivity as an exile; even her infants were smashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her nobility; all her dignitaries were bound with chains.
NET.11: You too will act like drunkards; you will go into hiding; you too will seek refuge from the enemy.
NET.12: All your fortifications will be like fig trees with first-ripe fruit: If they are shaken, their figs will fall into the mouth of the eater!
NET.13: Your warriors will be like women in your midst; the gates of your land will be wide open to your enemies; fire will consume the bars of your gates.
NET.14: Draw yourselves water for a siege! Strengthen your fortifications! Trample the mud and tread the clay! Make mud bricks to strengthen your walls!
NET.15: There the fire will consume you; the sword will cut you down; it will devour you like the young locust would. Multiply yourself like the young locust; multiply yourself like the flying locust!
NET.16: Increase your merchants more than the stars of heaven! They are like the young locust which sheds its skin and flies away.
NET.17: Your courtiers are like locusts, your officials are like a swarm of locusts! They encamp in the walls on a cold day, yet when the sun rises, they fly away; and no one knows where they are.
NET.18: Your shepherds are sleeping, O king of Assyria! Your officers are slumbering! Your people are scattered like sheep on the mountains and there is no one to regather them!
NET.19: Your destruction is like an incurable wound; your demise is like a fatal injury! All who hear what has happened to you will clap their hands for joy, for no one ever escaped your endless cruelty!
